title: Clementine Douglas Announces Debut Australian Headline Shows
summary: Earlier this year, Douglas made her Madison Square Garden debut alongside Dom Dolla.
contentText:
Clementine Douglas , the British singer, songwriter and producer whose voice has powered some of dance music’s biggest recent records, has announced her first Australian headline tour, set for two shows this September.

Douglas will play Sydney’s Oxford Art Factory on Sept. 23 and Melbourne’s The Night Cat on Sept. 25. A Live Nation presale opens Aug. 13 at 10 a.m. local time, with general tickets on sale Aug. 14 at 11 a.m. The run marks her first headline dates in the country, following a guest appearance alongside Dom Dolla during his Sydney show last year.

The tour announcement coincides with Douglas’ new single “Trust,” a self-written, self-produced and self-performed release that she describes as confronting the emotional chaos of modern dating. It continues her transition into the spotlight as a solo artist after years as one of dance music’s most in-demand collaborators.

That collaborative résumé has made Douglas a fixture on Billboard’s Hot Dance/Electronic Songs chart. Her most successful entry is “Blessings” with Calvin Harris , which debuted at No. 3 in May 2025 — the highest debut on the chart that week, opening with 2.9 million U.S. streams.

She first charted with Dom Dolla’s “Miracle Maker,” which peaked at No. 35 in 2022, was certified gold in Australia and named BBC Radio 1’s Hottest Record in the World on release, followed by “Asking” with Sonny Fodera and MK, which reached No. 44 in 2023.

Beyond the charts, Douglas has lent her voice to a roster of dance and electronic heavyweights, including David Guetta, Chase & Status, MJ Cole, Hannah Wants and The Blessed Madonna, and earned a BRIT Award nomination. Earlier this year, she made her Madison Square Garden debut, joining Dom Dolla onstage during his two sold-out nights at the venue — the Australian producer’s first shows there — to perform their collaborations “Miracle Maker” and “Saving Up” in front of more than 30,000 fans across the two nights.

The Australian shows arrive as dance music continues one of its strongest commercial runs in years, with vocal-driven house and its associated producers dominating festival bills and streaming charts globally.

Clementine Douglas — Australia 2026

Sept. 23 — Sydney — Oxford Art Factory

Sept. 25 — Melbourne — The Night Cat
